adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:47 — Switching process_detectors/evaluate to return a dict silently drops the previous duplicate-group-key detection and error logging (test_state_results_multi_group_dupe was deleted) without any replacement safeguard, reducing observability if a handler ever emits duplicate group keys.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `DetectorHandler.evaluate` is changed to return a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (and `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` now builds a dict). A dict cannot contain duplicate keys, so the prior duplicate-group-key detection in `process_detectors` (which was needed when `evaluate` returned a list) is no longer applicable. The deleted `test_state_results_multi_group_dupe` aligns with the new API shape (`group_vals` is now a dict as well), making the finding’s “handler emits duplicate group keys” scenario not verifiable under the new contract from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:243 — Removed `logger.error("Duplicate detector state group keys found", ...)` means a group-key collision (e.g. a StatefulDetectorHandler subclass bug producing the same `result.group_key` for two different inputs) now silently overwrites one result in the dict with no log/metric, eliminating the only production signal for this bug class

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the `DetectorHandler.evaluate` contract from returning a list to returning a dict keyed by `DetectorGroupKey` (`process_detectors` now iterates `detector_results.values()`). As a result, the previous duplicate-key detection/logging in `process_detectors` is removed. While `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` builds results from `group_values.items()` (a dict) and *normally* cannot produce duplicate keys, a buggy handler could still return two results with the same `result.group_key` (e.g., `evaluate_group_key_value` returning an incorrect/constant `group_key`), and the dict assignment (`results[result.group_key] = result`) would silently overwrite one without any log/metric. This is a real, diff-grounded loss of diagnostic/guard behavior, but it only manifests under handler bugs rather than guaranteed normal-path incorrectness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:299 — build_occurrence_and_event_data` (abstract, subclass-implemented) is called with no try/except inside `evaluate_group_key_value`; any exception propagates through `evaluate()` (line 58) and out of the `for detector in detectors:` loop in `process_detectors` (line 52), aborting processing (and `commit_state_updates`) for every remaining detector in the batch instead of failing just the one detector/group_key

adjudication.rationale: In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` the new else-branch calls the subclass hook `self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` with no local error handling. `process_detectors` also does not wrap `handler.evaluate(data_packet)` in try/except, so an exception from a single detector/group_key will abort the entire `for detector in detectors:` loop and skip processing remaining detectors in that batch. However, the finding’s mention of skipping `commit_state_updates` for remaining detectors is not verifiable from this diff, since `process_detectors` shown here does not call `commit_state_updates` at all.
